record.context_brief: Generic spectral uniqueness of lens spaces
record.original_question: Is a generic lens space spectrally unique, meaning that within an appropriate family of lens spaces it has no non-isometric partner with the same Laplace spectrum?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.5. Is a “generic” lens space spectrally unique?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lens space is defined as follows. Fix integers $n\ge 1$ and $q\ge 2$, and choose integers $p_1,\dots,p_n$ coprime to $q$. Let $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/q}$ and let the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ act on the unit sphere $S^{2n-1}\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ by
$$k\cdot (z_1,\dots,z_n) = (\zeta^{kp_1}z_1,\dots,\zeta^{kp_n}z_n).$$
This action is free and isometric with respect to the round metric, and the quotient $L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)=S^{2n-1}/(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ is a closed Riemannian manifold, called a lens space. Two lens spaces are isospectral if their Laplace–Beltrami operators on functions have the same eigenvalue spectrum (with multiplicities), and they are isometric if they are isometric as Riemannian manifolds. A lens space $L$ is called spectrally unique within the family of lens spaces (of given dimension $2n-1$ and fundamental-group order $q$) if every lens space isospectral to $L$ is in fact isometric to $L$.

Question: Is a generic lens space spectrally unique? That is, does there exist a natural notion of genericity in the parameter family $\{L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)\}$ such that, for a generic choice of parameters, the lens space $L(q;p_1,\dots,p_n)$ admits no non-isometric isospectral partner among lens spaces?
artifact.status_search_result: The literature has established spectral uniqueness in specific cases (e.g., three-dimensional lens spaces, homogeneous lens spaces, and certain p-form spectra), and explicit isospectral non-isometric pairs are known in higher dimensions. However, no source found establishes spectral uniqueness for a "generic" lens space in a precise general sense; the question is posed as an open problem in the spectral-geometry literature on lens spaces.

status_evidence.title: The spectrum on p-forms of a lens space
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit description of the spectrum of the Hodge–Laplace operator on lens spaces, with characterizations of isospectral pairs.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral uniqueness is known in special cases but the generic case remains a problem of interest.

status_evidence.title: On lens spaces which are isospectral but not isometric
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of non-isometric isospectral lens spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Isospectral non-isometric lens spaces exist, motivating the genericity question.

status_evidence.title: Spectra of lens spaces (arXiv:1504.03121)
status_evidence.snippet: Three-dimensional lens spaces are determined by their Laplace spectrum among lens spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Spectral uniqueness holds in dimension 3 but the generic higher-dimensional case is not settled.
